title: Soul of Cinder
snippet:
Soul of Cinder -  Dark Souls III - boss - lore 
 lore : The Soul of Cinder is the deific manifestation of the souls of all those who have linked themselves to the First Flame through history, becoming Lords of Cinder, and thus is an entity possessing all the abilities of the previous Champions despite just being an empty husk.

It exists as the Flame's last defense inside its Kiln, protecting it from anyone attempting to link it again and acting as the ultimate test of their strength—a role that it has enacted for a very long time, confronting all who entered the Kiln as aspiring Lords.

When tested by an aspiring Champion, the Soul of Cinder would even bring out the remnants of the will and power of the first one to ever link the First Flame: Lord Gwyn himself.

title: Soul of Cinder
snippet:
Soul of Cinder -  Dark Souls III - boss - description 
 description : The Soul of Cinder appears as a tall warrior wearing badly worn and charred armor. Its weapon of choice is the Firelink Greatsword, a larger version of the Coiled Sword, that can change its shape to suit its wielder's needs. It changes attack moves very smoothly, making it hard for players to counterattack it. The different fighting tactics make for a very memorable boss fight.

When the player first enters the arena, the Soul of Cinder will be sitting in the middle of the area, its sword planted before him within the First Flame, as if resting at a bonfire. As the player comes closer, the Soul of Cinder pulls the sword out of the ground and engages the player.

 lead : The **Soul of Gwyn, Lord of Cinder** (薪の王グウィンのソウル) is a consumable item in *Dark Souls.*

The boss soul of Gwyn, Lord of Cinder, is unique in that, as Gwyn is the final boss of *Dark Souls*, which ends shortly after the fight, its only use within the same play-through in which it was acquired is its immediate consumption, although it can be kept into New Game +, where it can be used to forge a unique weapon, or, in another unique occurrence , be traded for a unique miracle.

During the second phase, he can roll and dodge ranged attacks.
The Soul of Cinder has a fifth weapon style that goes unused, involving a greatsword. It covers both the body of the Soul of Cinder and the weapon in flames much like his final phase (for a video see here: http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ruKjgqhUr4A&t=14m50s). Whether it was part of its first phase, second phase, or something in-between is unknown.
Due to how the Soul of Cinder took on Gwyn's moveset and persona for his second phase, it could be inferred that one's prominence within the Soul of Cinder is related to the strength of their soul. This could also explain why the Soul of Cinder's armor strongly resembles the Elite Knight Set that the Chosen Undead was depicted as wearing in most *Dark Souls* art; as the Chosen Undead had slain the original Lords and most likely absorbed their souls, their soul would possess immense strength by the time they linked the Flame (if they indeed chose to do so).

Can't be either parried or spell-parried.
The Firelink Set can be purchased from the Shrine Handmaid once the Soul of Cinder has been defeated. If player purchased one before going to the next NG cycle, next one will appear in the following cycle.

title: Lords of Cinder
snippet:
The original Lord of Cinder was Gwyn, although more would link the flame and extend the Age of Fire in subsequent eras. Becoming a Lord of Cinder entails a sacrifice, as the Lord is consumed by the First Flame in the process. After Gwyn linked the flame, only his mere husk defended it; with each subsequent linking of the Flame, remnants of each new Lord of Cinder would merge with the previous ones' and strengthen the First Flame's guardian, eventually taking the form of the Soul of Cinder.

Throughout history, countless aspiring Lords were lost attempting to reach the Flame; among those who succeeded, some ultimately lacked the strength to withstand its power, and were burned to ash by the Flame instead of linking it. These individuals came to be known as Unkindled: ill-fated champions who were buried in the Cemetery of Ash, a graveyard which scarcely saw any visitors.

title: First Flame
snippet: By the time of *Dark Souls III*, many other such sacrifices, who have become posthumously known as Lords of Cinder, have given themselves to the First Flame, and the Age of Fire has persevered for many generations as a result. However, when the latest individual chosen for the honour, Prince Lothric, abandons his duty by refusing to link the fire, a desperate attempt to save the fading Flame begins. Four previous Lords of Cinder are resurrected to link the fire once more, however - aside from Ludleth of Courland - they too choose to flee their duties, forcing the Ashen One to drag them back.

title: Soul of Cinder
snippet:
Soul of Cinder -  Dark Souls III - boss - phase_1 
 phase_1 : Soul of Cinder can use four different weapon stances, each utilizing different skills and attacks based on a magic type in the game (excluding hexes).
***Standard (straight sword)**: It's default stance combines quick slashes and thrust attacks at range. Utilizes two unique weapon skills, one being an enhanced version of "stance", a "guard breaking" slash with increased range, and another which is two slow, but powerful, spin attacks.
***Scimitar/Pyromancy**: Quick, horizontal slashes and wound-up vertical slashes, and a quick, evasive slash or backflip to avoid attacks and can parry attacks and deliver a riposte. Also uses a combination of many offensive pyromancies, including Power Within, Great Combustion, Great Chaos Fire Orb and Poison Mist.

title: Lords of Cinder
snippet: By the events of *Dark Souls III*, Prince Lothric, who was raised to become a Lord of Cinder, refused to link the First Flame. This led to Lords of Cinder from the past being exhumed from their graves: these Lords were meant to sacrifice themselves to the Flame once again, using what little embers remained within themselves as kindling. However, most of these Lords refused the call, and instead settled back into their domains. To prevent the First Flame from dying out, the Unkindled would then be resurrected as a last resort; these Champions were bound to seek the absconded Lords of Cinder, and forcefully bring them back—in the form of their cinders—to their empty thrones at Firelink Shrine. Once all five Lords "sat" their thrones, an Unkindled Champion would be bestowed the embers of these Lords, and sent to the Kiln of the First Flame to overcome the final challenge and link the Flame.

title: Lords of Cinder
snippet:
Lords of Cinder -  Dark Souls III - character - lore 
 lore : The Lords of Cinder are beings that have linked the First Flame and prolonged the Age of Fire through the centuries. Although many of these champions have followed the sacrifice of Gwyn, Lord of Cinder, not everyone became a Lord of Cinder through heroic deeds or even of free will. One such case is Aldrich, who became a Lord only because he had the strength to become one, despite having obtained such power by devouring an untold number of humans for his own pleasure.

The continuous linking of the Flame eventually culminated in the Soul of Cinder, the deific manifestation of the souls of all those who linked the Flame throughout history. This being, although appearing as an empty husk, inherits the abilities of the Lords of Cinders who have come before. It has long existed as the Flame's last defense inside the Kiln, protecting it from Champions attempting to link it again and acting as the ultimate test of their strength.

title: Spirit (Dark Souls)
snippet:
Spirit (Dark Souls) -  Dark Souls - mechanic - appearance 
 appearance : Spirits appear as transparent light blue hollowed figures. They do not wear any armor and do not directly show what equipment that player was wearing. Instead what weapons they carry represent what class of weapon they actually have. Quivers and Bolt Quivers can also be seen if they are equipped. Spirits also ignore the aspects of character creation, and all use the *Average* body type, while all males are represented with the *Receding* hairstyle, and all females are represented with the *Ponytail A* hairstyle.

While most of the time a spirit's appearance is left vague and undefined, their true form can be seen when they approach within range of a bonfire.

title: Quelana of Izalith
snippet: Following the destruction of the Bed of Chaos, Quelana appears to have returned to Izalith, or what remains of it, at some point. Within the Demon Ruins, now neighbouring the Catacombs of Carthus, Quelana's pyromancy tome is found on a corpse clutching onto what seems like the petrified corpse of her sister. If these two fossils are indeed those of Quelana and the Fair Lady, it would show that Quelana ultimately ended her self-imposed exile to be reunited with her last extant sister, in the final hours of her life.

title: Age of Dark
snippet: of Fire had become a twisted shadow of its former self. As a result of the prolonging of the current Age, the act of which seemingly constituted a rejection of the natural order, the material world had become irreparably corrupted, and all lands from all previous points in time had begun to converge upon a single point: the Kingdom of Lothric. Upon reviving and seeing what had become of the world they had fought to protect, the Lords of Cinder, too, rejected the linking of the Flame and refused to sit upon their thrones. title: Ending (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
Ending (Dark Souls III) -  Dark Souls III - mechanic - lead 
 lead : __NOTOC__

There are four **endings to *Dark Souls III***.

All four endings require the Ashen One to first gather the cinders of four great lords to reach the Kiln of the First Flame, where they must defeat the Soul of Cinder. Only the first ending does not require actions beyond strictly the main questline, although it is possible for up to three to be available simultaneously at the Kiln. All endings revolve around the First Flame, symbolized by a special bonfire that can be interacted with upon slaying the Soul of Cinder.

title: Rusted Coin (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
Rusted Coin (Dark Souls III) -  Dark Souls III - item - notes 
 notes : Effect stacks with other items that boosts Item Discovery.
Using this coin along with the Symbol of Avarice, the Covetous Gold Serpent Ring +3, and the Crystal Sage's Rapier will increase Item Discovery up to 315 units.
Can be used on ladders.
Copper does not rust, though it does oxidize, becoming green or bluish green. This is very likely what is covering most of the coin.

title: Bone Scythe
snippet:
Bone Scythe -  Dark Souls II - weapon - description 
 description : Scythe forged from the soul of the Covetous Demon.

The curved spine of the Covetous Demon is as hard as rock, and rather than slicing through flesh, this weapon seems to grind it apart.

That thing that ended up a monstrous fiend, what was it to begin with, and why did it never leave the queen? Perhaps it was entranced by some perversion of love.

title: Herald Set
snippet:
What is most peculiar of this set is that the cloth garments are not as reliable as the game states them to be, with the gloves and leggings both having terrible absorption in what they should protect more effectively against lightning and strike damage.

It is best to replace both of the gloves and leggings with a more suitable, protective choice in those slots, to help balance out the set's drawbacks more efficiently.

title: Dark Lord
snippet: Contrary to what the title itself might convey, the Dark Lord is not necessarily a malevolent force. Rather, it merely refers to the Dark Soul found within all Humans, an antithesis to the First Flame and the sunlight of Gwyn. According to Primordial Serpent Kaathe, the Dark Lord is prophesied to bring down the reign of the Anor Londo gods and their "unnatural" world order, liberating Humans from the oppression of the Darksign and the curse of the Undead.

title: Great Chaos Fireball
snippet:
Great Chaos Fireball -  Dark Souls - spell - general_information 
 general_information : The player hurls a giant fireball, which does a large amount of damage on impact with a good area of effect, identical to Great Fireball. The fireball has a fire attack power of 3.0 times the Pyromancy Flame's magic adjust and the lava pool has a fire attack power of 2.0 times the Pyromancy Flame's magic adjust.

Contrary to what the name suggests, Great Chaos Fireball does not scale with the player's amount of humanity (like Chaos weapons do). It can only be improved by upgrading and ascending the Pyromancy Flame used to cast it.

title: Crimson Set
snippet:
Crimson Set -  Dark Souls - armor - plot 
 plot : The set is worn by Ingward and the other two sealers of New Londo, Yulva and one of Lautrec of Carim's unnamed companions, although said companion does not wear the head piece. The Mask of the Sealer symbolizes the resolve of the sealers to keep the seal shut and to demonstrate their atonement for those sacrificed in the process of sealing what is now the New Londo Ruins. The set that the player finds likely once belonged to Yulva, as her sorcery, Remedy, is found with it.

title: Timeline
snippet:
The Ashen One is suddenly confronted by Slave Knight Gael, who reached the end of time and devoured the Dark Soul from the pygmy nobles to bring it to the young painter
The Ashen One defeats Gael and obtains the mass of Dark Soul contained in his blood and brinks it back to the young painter in the painted world
The Ashen One, before resuming their journey, learns how the young painter will now be able, using Flame and Darkness, to create a new painted world
The Ashen One, during their journey, obtains an immense amount of souls, reaching the power necessary to link the First Flame
The Ashen One, reaches the First Flame but is confronted by the Soul of Cinder, the manifestation of the previous Lords of Cinder who had linked it and now protect it as its last defense
The Ashen One defeats the Soul of Cinder and gains access to the First Flame

title: Azal, Sage of Forossa
snippet:
Azal, Sage of Forossa -  Dark Souls II - character - lore 
 lore : Azal was an accomplished sage of Forossa, one of the Northwarders who earn their title after surviving a journey of great hardship. He was exceptionally skilled as he imbued his staff with magic, granting it unique powers. This made the tool unwieldy for the inexperienced, which proved the sage's magical prowess.

What became of him is unknown, but his staff can be retrieved on a corpse in Eleum Loyce, a kingdom ruled by a Forossan champion. It's possible, then, that Azal died in the frozen city, perhaps while investigating what had happened to it.
